demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Triggers.value: Sleeping alone or in an unfamiliar place
A specific texture associated with the event

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Watching TV programmes/ films or reading about similar events
I dwell on how the event could have been prevented
perform mental rituals to prevent bad things from happening again

Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
I have failed in my most important role in life

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: For trauma involving the unexpected death of a loved one, 'being forced to do something' is a hard-to-explain primary trigger unless there is additional trauma context not represented elsewhere. The other items suggest grief-related and generalized alarm reactions rather than a coercion/autonomy theme.

issues.item: Triggers: Tactile (Texture): A specific texture associated with the event
issues.explanation: A highly specific texture cue is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile and this trauma type unless the death involved a distinctive sensory scene. No memory items or appraisals anchor such a sensory trigger, so it feels disconnected from the formulation.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: Alarm to nearby movement fits better with assault/combat-style threat than bereavement after a loved one's death. In this profile, the threat items cluster around immediate physical danger, but the appraisals are dominated by grief, role failure, and meaning loss, creating a cross-node mismatch.

issues.item: Triggers: Tactile (Texture): A specific texture associated with the event
issues.explanation: For traumatic bereavement, a texture-specific trigger is hard to reconcile unless the death involved a very distinctive tactile cue; nothing else in the profile supports a tactile trauma context, so this item is clinically difficult to integrate.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat profile is dominated by movement/touch startle and hypervigilance, which fits assault/combat-type danger more than bereavement. In the absence of memory content or appraisals tied to interpersonal attack or bodily danger, this item is a poor fit with the stated trauma.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: Alarm to unexpected touch similarly implies a bodily threat context not represented elsewhere in the profile. With traumatic death of a loved one, this is not impossible, but alongside the other items it creates a threat pattern that is hard to explain from the trauma formulation given.

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: The trigger 'being forced to do something' is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma of unexpected death of a loved one. It implies a coercive/interpersonal-control trauma theme that is not otherwise represented in the profile.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat items focused on sudden nearby movement and unexpected touch suggest a trauma pattern centered on imminent physical assault or attack. That is difficult to integrate with bereavement-focused trauma unless there is corroborating content elsewhere, which is absent here.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: The appraisal 'I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible' introduces a violent-loss-of-control theme that is not supported by the rest of the bereavement profile and does not connect clearly to the selected triggers or memory content.
